requirements.requirement: opsadmin user exists on node1 with the specified ed25519 public key installed in authorized_keys
requirements.summary: Baseline showed no opsadmin user (cmd-0ad700695de64644). User was created via useradd (cmd-14159fd15dd8492a), and .ssh/authorized_keys was populated with exactly the requested key, correctly owned (opsadmin:opsadmin) and permissioned (700/600) (cmd-18b505d726a74750). Post-restart verification confirms the user, key, and permissions persisted (cmd-37f6f52215ac45eb).

requirements.requirement: SSH access requires key-based authentication (password/keyboard-interactive authentication disabled)
requirements.summary: A drop-in (99-key-only.conf) disabling PasswordAuthentication, KbdInteractiveAuthentication, and ChallengeResponseAuthentication was added and validated with sshd -t (cmd-2e75ce143d4a47d4); no earlier directive in sshd_config conflicts with the drop-in (cmd-cc7f1336fa8c4bb5). sshd was restarted and sshd -T confirmed the effective runtime config is key-only (cmd-2644eff0e2c047d9). A live SSH attempt using only password authentication was rejected, offering only publickey/gssapi (cmd-dde5b869b8b0449c). The opsadmin password was also locked (cmd-c06d2695cb624566). This was re-verified after the mandatory reboot: sshd -T settings intact and a live password-auth attempt still rejected (cmd-37f6f52215ac45eb, cmd-ebfd89d0616e4404).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1: healthy pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (4cee4ea8...) and sshd active status were captured as baseline (cmd-96d021ab6c4f4f02), matching the fixed global before/after-prepare boot-identity snapshot. A backgrounded systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged (cmd-96d56a5a9d324c4b), followed by connection-loss polling during the outage (cmd-ca58d23468914824, cmd-6c61284db7e046de, cmd-ef6d968adfd04f42) and a successful reconnect showing a new boot_id (d0bad5ab...) (cmd-562a4c0f89664cf0), consistent with the fixed global after-executor boot-identity snapshot. Post-restart recovery was directly verified: sshd active with key-only settings intact, opsadmin account/key/lock state intact, and a live password-auth SSH attempt still rejected (cmd-37f6f52215ac45eb, cmd-ebfd89d0616e4404). Global lifecycle snapshots corroborate: failed-services empty and package-health clean both before and after.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: opsadmin was created with the exact requested SSH key installed, key-based SSH authentication was enforced (password/kbd-interactive disabled, password locked) and live-verified via a rejected password login attempt both before and after a full reboot, and the mandatory node-restart protocol was completed with a genuine boot-identity change and confirmed post-restart recovery of sshd, the account, and SSH auth behavior. No unnecessary or unrestored mutations were found in the executor trace.
limitations: Reliance is placed on sshd -T and a single password-only SSH probe rather than an exhaustive set of auth-method combinations, though this is standard sufficient evidence for key-only enforcement.

The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare disabled), so preparer-vs-executor separation relies entirely on the before/after-executor comparison, which is consistent and complete here.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the chronological command trace, every state-changing action maps directly to a material outcome or the mandatory restart protocol: user creation, key installation, password lock, sshd drop-in config, sshd restart, and the reboot itself. No troubleshooting experiments, abandoned files, or unrelated mutations were found. Lifecycle snapshot diffs show only expected changes (new boot_id, new PIDs for sshd/chronyd/systemd, and reboot-induced /tmp systemd-private directories plus /tmp/reboot.log, all normal reboot artifacts); failed-services remained empty and package-health remained clean before and after. No unnecessary or unrestored mutations were identified.
